applies_why: Yes: it resolves a pressed witness, Luke 2:48-49, by treating Mary's phrase as qualified by the child's next phrase rather than weighing the pressed chain against the link by footing.
quote: Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: I weighed "never verse by verse": (1) as barring phrase-level qualification within a pressed verse when the witnesses are a chain, and (2) as allowing such immediate-context qualification if it is not the retired stating-verse test.
why: The judge uses a verse-level qualification of Luke 2:48-49 instead of a chain-against-chain footing analysis, which K-C forbids when the pressed witnesses are read together.
